resources.string: What the app stores and shares.

CatSmoker is an open-source Android app with no accounts, no sign-in and no project-operated servers. Almost everything the app knows stays on your device. This policy explains what is stored locally, what the app\u2019s third-party SDKs send, and what rights you have. CatSmoker is the \u201cService Provider\u201d referred to below.

Settings and app state are kept in on-device storage only: theme, language, onboarding choices, launch counters, ad preferences, update-check preferences, game library entries, spoofing profiles and per-app assignments, Gaming Mode options (DNS choice, refresh rate, cleaner patterns, suspend lists), overlay and crosshair positions, game-config backups, diagnostic logs and crash records. Nothing in this list is uploaded to the developer — there is no backend to upload it to. Uninstalling the app, or clearing its data, deletes it.

The app bundles Firebase Analytics (Google Analytics for Firebase) in both builds. Unless you turn it off, it sends Google automatic usage events (app opens, sessions, app updates and app exceptions) together with the app version, device model, language and a per-install identifier; Google also estimates an approximate location from your IP address. The app itself logs no custom events, so game titles, file paths, configuration contents and values you type are never sent. Firebase may also read the advertising identifier, as the ad SDKs do. Collection is on by default. The switch under Settings > Send Analytics Data is saved on the device, re-applied to the SDK at every startup and applied immediately when changed; while it is off, no analytics events are sent. Neither build sets cookies or runs web pixels. The Firebase installations service may still contact Google to keep an installation ID current, and Google handles that data under its own privacy policy.

Ads depend on the build. The full (GitHub) build shows banner ads from Start.io and has a free ads-off switch in Settings. The Play Store build shows ads from AdMob and lets you remove them with a one-time Google Play purchase. The ad SDK starts with the app and may collect your advertising ID, device information and IP address to serve and measure ads, under that provider\u2019s policy. Turning ads off or buying ad removal stops banners being requested and shown; it does not remove the SDK from the app.

When you tap \u201cCheck for Updates\u201d (or when automatic checks run), the app queries the public GitHub releases API for this project. That request necessarily reveals your IP address and app version to GitHub, under GitHub\u2019s own privacy terms. In the full build automatic checks are on by default and can be turned off in Settings; the Play Store build never checks GitHub for updates. Downloaded update files are stored in the app\u2019s private external files directory and installed only after you confirm.
5. Logs, profiles and files you choose to share

Diagnostic logs, crash reports, exported profiles and game configs never leave the device on their own. They are exported only when you tap Share or Export, through Android\u2019s share sheet or a file picker, to a destination you choose. Logs can contain device and system details — review them before sending them to anyone.

The app requests permissions only to perform the features you ask for: file access for reading and backing up game configs, overlay permission for the performance and crosshair overlays, usage access to detect game sessions, notification access for Gaming Mode quiet-hours, microphone access only for the optional audio-visualizer boost, and Bluetooth information only to identify audio devices. Each can be denied — the related feature then reports itself as unavailable instead of failing silently.

The optional app-network firewall uses Android\u2019s VPN framework as a local on-device filter. Traffic rules are applied on the phone itself; no traffic is sent to project servers, because there are none.

Community links (GitHub, website, Discord, Telegram) and donation options (PayPal, Binance, crypto addresses) open outside the app. When you use them, those services receive the data they normally collect (such as your IP address and, for payments, your payment details) under their own policies. Donations are voluntary and processed entirely by those external services — the app never sees or stores your payment information.

You can ask the developer to access, correct or delete personal data the developer holds about you — in practice, support emails and any files you chose to send — and you can withdraw consent at any time without affecting processing already carried out. Write to catsmoker.lab@gmail.com. Data held by Google or Start.io is controlled by those providers; use their privacy tools or ask the developer for the right contact. California residents (CCPA/CPRA) have the right to know what personal information is collected, to delete it, to opt out of its sale or sharing, and not to be discriminated against for exercising these rights. The developer does not sell personal information and does not receive your raw analytics or advertising data; the providers named above may share identifiers for advertising under their own policies. Send CCPA/CPRA requests to catsmoker.lab@gmail.com.

Data may be disclosed when required by law, such as to comply with a subpoena or similar legal process, or when the developer believes in good faith that disclosure is necessary to protect rights, safety or the safety of others, investigate fraud, or respond to a government request. Providers that work for the developer — for example the email service behind the support inbox — process data only for that purpose and under confidentiality obligations. The developer does not receive your raw app data from Firebase or the ad SDKs, only aggregated reports.

Google (Firebase, AdMob, Google Play) and Start.io may process data in countries outside your own, including outside the European Economic Area. Where the law requires safeguards for such transfers, those providers use mechanisms such as Standard Contractual Clauses approved by the European Commission, adequacy decisions, or your consent where required and legally permitted. The developer\u2019s own correspondence is handled by email providers that may store it abroad. Data protection laws in other countries may differ from those where you live.

Data on your device stays until you uninstall the app or clear its data. Support emails and files you send are kept until you ask for deletion, or longer where the law requires it. Firebase and the ad providers keep data under their own retention policies; the developer cannot delete data held by them on your behalf — use their privacy controls or contact them. Aggregated statistics that no longer identify you may be kept indefinitely.

The app is not intended for children under 16, or the higher age required where you live, and the developer does not knowingly collect personal data from children or market the app to them. If a child has sent personal data — for example in an email — a parent or guardian can write to catsmoker.lab@gmail.com and it will be deleted. Where parental or guardian consent is required by law, the app is not intended for use without that consent.

App data is protected by Android\u2019s app sandbox and your device lock. The developer operates no server that stores app data, so there is no central user database to breach; support emails are protected by the email provider\u2019s security. If a breach affects personal data the developer holds, affected users will be notified as required by law, including the nature of the breach and the steps taken to address it.

Optional features — overlays, the VPN filter, root or Shizuku actions and sharing — run only when you turn them on. You can withdraw consent by turning a feature off or uninstalling the app; this does not affect processing carried out before withdrawal. Uninstalling stops the app from collecting data on your device, but does not delete data already sent to Google or Start.io. To request deletion of data the developer holds, email catsmoker.lab@gmail.com.

The developer may update this policy from time to time. The current version always ships in the app on this screen with a new \u201clast updated\u201d date. Material changes are announced by posting the new text here; where the law requires consent to a material change, it will be requested before the change takes effect. Previous versions are available on request at catsmoker.lab@gmail.com.
Questions about this policy, privacy requests, and reports of unlawful content or misuse can be sent to catsmoker.lab@gmail.com. The developer will respond within a reasonable period.
